annotations.description: World Breaker is arguably the strongest card among the 4 being put on the bottom (a 5/7 reach trampler with artifact/enchantment destruction). Placing it bottommost means it will be the last of these cards drawn. In a game where the player has expensive threats like Ghalta and Colossal Dreadmaw, World Breaker could be excellent in the late game. Planar Atlas (ramp) might be more immediately useful and could have been placed closer to bottom instead.
annotations.actionTaken: Put World Breaker as the bottommost card of the library
annotations.betterLine: Put Blisterpod at the bottom (weakest card) and keep World Breaker closer to the top of the bottom cards, with Planar Atlas also relatively accessible for ramp purposes

annotations.description: On turn 6 with only 2 lands in play and a hand full of 3-6+ mana creatures, the player declined to play Ash Barrens as their land for the turn. This keeps them stuck at 2 mana when they desperately need to hit land drops to cast Thrashing Brontodon (3 mana), Ornery Dilophosaur (4 mana), or Warden of Geometries (4 mana). Meanwhile the opponent is developing their board with Elvish Warmaster and tokens.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing Ash Barrens, staying at 2 lands on turn 6.
annotations.betterLine: Play Ash Barrens as a land to get to 3 mana sources, enabling Thrashing Brontodon next turn or using the extra mana toward other spells.

annotations.description: Missed a critical land drop while stuck on only 3 lands with a hand full of expensive creatures (3-12 mana). The opponent is developing their board with Elvish Warmaster and tokens, and every turn without deploying threats puts Timmy further behind. With Thrashing Brontodon at 3 mana and Ornery Dilophosaur/Warden at 4, this land drop was essential to start deploying creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing Ash Barrens as a land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Ash Barrens to have 4 lands, enabling Thrashing Brontodon next turn (1GG with 3 green sources) or setting up 4-drops the following turn.

annotations.description: Passed on casting Might of the Masses during combat with all opponent's lands tapped and no blockers. This would have dealt 3 extra damage (from +3/+3 with 3 creatures) for just 1 green mana with zero risk, bringing the opponent from 12 to 9 life instead.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Might of the Masses, dealing only 6 damage instead of 9.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Might of the Masses targeting Ghirapur Guide (or any attacker) for +3/+3, dealing 9 total unblocked damage. The opponent is fully tapped out with no creatures, making this completely risk-free extra damage.

annotations.description: Missed lethal damage. Opponent is at 12 life with no untapped blockers (Brontodon is sick). Attacking with Elvish Warmaster (2/2), Ghirapur Guide (3/2), and Elf Warrior Token (1/1) deals 6 damage. But with 6 creatures on board and 1 untapped Forest, casting Might of the Masses on any attacker would give +6/+6, for a total of 12 damage — exactly lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Elvish Warmaster, Ghirapur Guide, and Elf Warrior Token for 6 damage, without planning to use Might of the Masses for lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with the same three creatures, then in the declare blockers step (or after no blocks), cast Might of the Masses on Ghirapur Guide (or any attacker) for +6/+6, dealing 12 total damage for exact lethal.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing 6 opponent creatures, Brood Monitor can't be cast this turn (needs 6 mana, only 5 available with land drop). Blisterpod costs just {G} and provides an immediate chump blocker this turn, plus creates a Scion token when it dies for additional blocking. At 2 life, surviving to next turn is not guaranteed.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Brood Monitor from Ancient Stirrings
annotations.betterLine: Take Blisterpod to deploy immediately as a chump blocker alongside Stalking Drone, maximizing blockers this turn at 2 life. Surviving one more turn is the priority before deploying expensive threats.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing a massive board of elves that will attack next turn, casting Warden of Geometries for 4 mana uses all available mana and provides a 2/3 body, while Stalking Drone for 2 mana provides a 2/2 that can pump to 3/4 with colorless mana from Warped Landscape, leaving 2 mana open for flexibility.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Warden of Geometries for {4}, using all remaining mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Stalking Drone for {1}{G}, leaving 2 mana open. The Drone can pump to 3/4 with Warped Landscape's {C}, making it a larger blocker than Warden's 2/3, while preserving mana for other options.

recent_chat: Opus Brewer: Commune with Dinosaurs, huh? That's a cool card for finding key pieces. I've been thinking about how Dinosaur tribal could work in different shells - curious what you're running!
Opus Brewer: Thriving Grove choosing Red? Gruul Dinos would be a sweet build. That Commune + ramp shell has real potential. Meanwhile I'm brewing up an Elf army over here 🌲
Opus Brewer: Might of the Masses with 6 creatures on board... this is exactly why Elf token generators and pump spells belong in the same deck! 🧪 GG?

Opus Brewer: Ghalta and Colossal Dreadmaw? Love that as a finisher package, but right now my elf army is doing the stomping! Dilophosaur is a sweet card though - deathtouch + potential 4/4 is such good deckbuilding value 🦖

Opus Brewer: The elf tribal engine is just too efficient for the dino ramp plan to stabilize. Warmaster generating tokens every turn is such a broken card for this shell - I need to remember this for future brews! GG 🌲🧝
